subject: literature
topic: Metre and versification: iambic, trochaic, couplet, quatrain, blank verse

kept.q: A poem has stanzas of three lines each, with all three lines rhyming together (aaa, bbb, ccc...). What is this stanza form called?
kept.explanation: A three-line stanza, whether or not all lines rhyme together, is called a tercet. A quatrain has four lines, a couplet has two, and a sestet has six.
kept.pidgin: Three lines stanza na tercet, whether dem rhyme abi dem no rhyme. Quatrain get four lines, couplet get two, and sestet get six.

kept.q: In prosody, what name is given to the practice of running a sentence or clause beyond the end of one line of poetry into the next, without a pause?
kept.explanation: Enjambment is when a thought continues from one poetic line to the next without a grammatical break. Caesura is a pause within a line, elision is dropping a sound, and scansion is the analysis of metre.
kept.pidgin: Enjambment na when sentence carry go another line without stopping. Caesura na pause inside line, and scansion na to check metre.

kept.q: Scan this line and identify its metrical pattern: 'The WIND blew HARD across the EMPty PLAIN.'
kept.explanation: The line has five feet, each rising from an unstressed to a stressed syllable (the WIND, blew HARD, across, the EMP, ty PLAIN), which is iambic pentameter. It is not tetrameter because there are five, not four, feet.
kept.pidgin: Dis line get five feet wey dey go from soft to strong sound, and dat one na iambic pentameter. E no be tetrameter because e get five feet, no be four.

kept.q: A dramatist writes a tragedy in which the noble characters speak in unrhymed iambic pentameter, while a comic servant character speaks entirely in ordinary prose. What literary purpose does this mixing most likely serve?
options: To show that the servant is more intelligent than the nobles
To mark a difference in social rank and tone between characters
To indicate that the play is poorly constructed
To prove that blank verse cannot express comedy
kept.explanation: Playwrights traditionally gave elevated blank verse to noble or serious characters and plain prose to lower-class or comic characters, marking social rank and shifting tone. This contrast is a deliberate stylistic device, not a flaw.
kept.pidgin: Playwrights dey use poetry for noble people and ordinary prose for servants to show dia social rank. Na style dem dey use, no be say play spoil.

kept.q: Read this quatrain: 'The farmer rises with the break of day, / He tills the soil beneath the mango tree, / His children laugh and romp along the way, / Their voices rise in simple, joyful glee.' What is the rhyme scheme of this stanza?
kept.explanation: Lines one and three rhyme (day/way) and lines two and four rhyme (tree/glee), giving an alternating abab pattern. This is different from couplet rhyme (aabb) or enclosed rhyme (abba).
kept.pidgin: Line one and three rhyme, and line two and four rhyme, so na abab pattern. E no be aabb or abba.

kept.q: Which of the following best explains why Milton chose blank verse rather than rhymed couplets for his long epic poem on the fall of man?
options: Blank verse is easier to memorise than rhymed verse
Blank verse allowed flexible, sustained argument without the constraint of finding rhymes over thousands of lines
Rhymed couplets cannot be written in iambic pentameter
Blank verse has no fixed syllable count, making it simpler to write
kept.explanation: Blank verse keeps the regular iambic pentameter rhythm but frees the poet from hunting for rhymes across a very long work, allowing natural, flowing argument. It still has a fixed ten-syllable, five-foot line, so the other options are wrong.
kept.pidgin: Blank verse help poet make e write long story easily without looking for rhyme every time. E still get ten syllables, so na correct choice.

kept.q: A student is asked to identify the smallest repeated unit of stressed and unstressed syllables used to measure the rhythm of a line of poetry. What is this unit called?
kept.explanation: The foot is the basic repeating unit of stressed and unstressed syllables, such as an iamb or a trochee, used to measure rhythm. Metre is the overall pattern formed by feet, while stanza and verse refer to larger groupings.
kept.pidgin: Foot na di small unit wey dem dey take measure rhythm for poetry. Metre na di whole pattern, while stanza and verse big pass am.

q.q: Consider two lines: Line 1 is written in strict iambic pentameter with a regular rhyme scheme. Line 2 has the same ten-syllable iambic pentameter rhythm but has no rhyme at all. What term distinguishes Line 2 from Line 1?
options: Line 2 is an example of free verse
Line 2 is an example of blank verse
Line 2 is an example of a heroic couplet
Line 2 is an example of a quatrain
Line 2 is an example of a villanelle
q.explanation: Blank verse keeps the regular iambic pentameter metre but drops rhyme, which matches Line 2 exactly. Free verse has no fixed metre at all, and heroic couplets and quatrains require rhyme, so they do not fit.
